verdict_b_source_and_test_quality.status: FAIL — late rotation failure can be misreported and retried against partially changed storage

findings.finding: The UI treats any rotateDeviceKey rejection as proof that rotation failed and tells the admin to try Re-key again, but the production operation is a multi-write sequence. It retires the previous history entry, generates a key, persists the new active key, then appends history and imports the key. If a later step rejects after the active-key write, the key has changed despite the failure alert; retrying can rotate again and can leave an active key without its history entry. The current test replaces rotateDeviceKey with a single rejecting/resolving mock and cannot expose this partial-commit state.
findings.required_resolution: Make rotation result recoverable/honest across partial storage failures, or reconcile persisted active key/history after rejection before offering retry. Add a forcing case at the real storage boundary where active-key persistence succeeds and a later step fails; prove retry cannot silently rotate a second time or strand the active key.
